subject: Agriculture
title: Water Table Collapse
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Water Table Collapse.

hook.text: Punjab's water table is dropping 1 meter per year. Rice paddies are drinking the aquifer dry.

buildup.text: Green Revolution rice in Punjab requires flooding fields for months. It was never meant for this climate.

discovery.text: Free electricity for pumps means farmers pay nothing to extract groundwater. There's no incentive to conserve.

twist.text: Some wells now reach 200 meters deep. Each year, pumps must work harder to pull water from lower aquifers.

climax.text: Scientists warn Punjab's groundwater could be functionally depleted within 25 years at current rates.

punchline.text: The Green Revolution quenched hunger but drained the wells.

quiz.question: How fast is Punjab's water table dropping?

details.summary: Intensive irrigation for Green Revolution crops has caused water tables to fall dramatically in key food-producing regions. This topic covers how groundwater depletion threatens Punjab, the North China Plain, the Ogallala Aquifer, and other regions that depend on wells for irrigation.
details.whyItMatters: Groundwater is being extracted at rates far exceeding natural recharge. In India's Punjab, the water table drops over one meter per year. When wells go dry, intensive agriculture collapses, threatening food security for billions who depend on.
takeaways: India extracts more groundwater than any country—over 250 billion cubic meters per year
Punjab's water table drops more than one meter annually due to rice-wheat irrigation
The Ogallala Aquifer has lost 30% of its volume since irrigation began in the 1950s

faq.question: Why is groundwater depletion accelerating in Green Revolution regions?
faq.answer: Green Revolution crops require reliable irrigation, and free or subsidized electricity encourages unlimited pumping in India. Pumping exceeds recharge by 2-3 times in many regions. As shallow wells dry up, farmers drill deeper, creating a race to the bottom that accelerates aquifer depletion.

faq.question: What happens when a major agricultural aquifer runs dry?
faq.answer: When wells dry up, irrigated agriculture collapses. Farmers lose their livelihoods, food prices spike, and mass rural migration follows. Parts of the Ogallala region have already returned to dryland farming. Saudi Arabia exhausted its fossil aquifer and largely abandoned domestic wheat production.
